patch_description: The original program uses simple/exponentially-weighted moving averages, which introduce fixed lag proportional to window size and pass noise-induced slope reversals. My novel approach replaces fixed smoothing windows with a two-state (level + slope) Kalman filter running causally over the samples, then reports window-anchored outputs (same output length/alignment as the sliding-window baseline). Key insights: (1) an explicit slope state lets the filter *predict* the next sample from the current trend, drastically reducing lag error versus backward-looking averages; (2) adaptive process noise (innovation-based, like adaptive Kalman/Sage-Husa estimators) makes the filter automatically tighten smoothing in quiet regions and react fast during genuine regime changes; (3) a slope-hysteresis smoothing stage suppresses false reversals by requiring the estimated slope to persistently exceed a noise-scaled deadzone before contributing to the output. This combines Kalman trend tracking with a trend-detection/hysteresis paradigm — fundamentally different from the weighted-average approach while keeping identical interface (process_signal, run_signal_processing, etc.).
